ex.t: 到去年为止，黄石地区的灰狼数量已增长到170多只。

ex.s: From technological solutions to educational campaigns, food producers and sellers are looking for ways to use more of what we’re already growing.
ex.t: 从技术解决方案到教育宣传活动，食物生产者和销售者正在寻找方法来更多地利用

ex.s: Instead, they grow better inside, where it is warmer
ex.t: 相反，它们在更温暖的室内长得更好

ex.s: But remember, it’s you that has to grow and read and reread in order to better understand your friends.
ex.t: 但请记住，是你自己需要成长、阅读和反复阅读，才能更好地理解你的朋友。

ex.s: Farmers in many countries are also adapting like this—either by growing new produce, or by growing the same things differently.
ex.t: 许多国家的农民也在这样适应——要么种植新的农产品，要么用不同的方式种植同样的东西

defs.def: to become too big to fit into a piece of clothing 孩子
to stop doing sth as you become older 因长大而改掉（或革除、戒除）某习惯

ex.s: You can plant a tree，make a meal with locally grown vegetables，or save power—the possibilities are endless.
ex.t: 你可以种一棵树，用当地种植的蕴菜做一顿饭，或者节省电力——可能性是无穷的。

ex.s: As I grew older and became a mother, the library took on a new place and an added meaning in my life.
ex.t: 随着我长大并成为母亲，图书馆在我的生活中有了新的位置和额外的意义。

defs.def: to develop from sth 产生于，源于（某事物）

ex.s: A few characters are used to create a single impression growing out of the theme.
ex.t: 少数人物被用来创造一种源于主题的单一印象。

defs.def: to develop into an adult 人
别那么幼稚；别耍小孩子脾气；变得老成些

ex.s: The jawbone didn’t have to do as much work and so didn’t grow to be so large.
ex.t: 颌骨不必那么用力，所以长得没那么大了。

defs.def: to develop gradually 逐渐发展；形成

ex.s: The friendship that grew out of the experience of making that film and The Sting four years later had its root in the fact that although there was an age difference, we both came from a tradition of theater and live TV.
ex.t: 从拍摄那部电影以及四年后拍摄《骗中骗》的经历中发展出来的友谊，其根源在于这样一个事实：尽管我们有年龄差距，但我们都来自戏剧和现场电视的传统。
